To apply the ratio test, we define ${a}_{n}=(-1)^{n+1}{4}^{n}{x}^{n+3}.$ Then, we calculate the ratio of two successive terms and take the limit as $n\to \infty :$

$$
\begin{aligned}L & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }|\frac{{a}_{n+1}}{{a}_{n}}| \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }|\frac{(-1)^{n+1}{4}^{n+1}{x}^{n+4}}{(-1)^{n}{4}^{n}{x}^{n+3}}| \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }|-4x| \\  & =4|x|\end{aligned}
$$

The series converges if $L<1.$ In this case, the convergence condition is satisfied if 

$$
4|x|<1\,⇒\,|x|<\frac{1}{4}.
$$

Therefore, we conclude that the radius of convergence is $R=\frac{1}{4}.$
